question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Din-i Ilahi.
question.text: The Din-i Ilahi was a new syncretic religion promulgated by Akbar, the ruler of this empire. This Muslim empire ruled over most of India under its last major emperor, Aurangzeb.
question.clue: This empire was founded after the defeat of Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat.

swap.leadin: Three prominent figures with this last name were assassinated by political and/or religious opponents inthe twentieth century.
swap.text: Give this shared surname of several figures in Indian political history, including Prime Minister Rajiv andindependence leader Mahatma.
swap.clue: A politician with this surname instituted forced sterilization and removed civil liberties during a period dubbed "The Emergency."

question.leadin: In a speech after an attack by Nathuram Godse, this politician declared "friends and comrades, the light has gone out of our lives."
question.text: Name this politician, who not even a year earlier gave his inaugural address titled "Tryst with Destiny." This politician was the first prime minister of a newly independent India.
question.clue: During a crisis over Kashmir, this man instructed his defense minister V.K. Menon to undertake an 8-hour filibuster in front of the U.N. Security Council.

swap.leadin: This man championed a policy of Satyagraha and led the Salt March before being assassinated by Nathuram Godse.
swap.text: Name this Indian nationalist leader, a champion of nonviolent civil disobedience.
swap.clue: This this man led a March to Dandi which led to a declaration of Pura Swaraj, or complete self-rule.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Battle of Plassey.
question.text: This organization, which built Fort William, won the Battle of Plassey under general Robert Clive. This joint-stock company was nationalized after the Sepoy Rebellion of 1857.
question.clue: One representative of this organization, Warren Hastings, reported on a 1770 famine caused by the policies of its official, Robert Clive.

swap.text: Company rule came to an end after this rebellion. The spark for this rebellion came after a rumor spread that the British greased their Enfield rifle cartridges with pig and cow fat.
swap.clue: This event, which led to the exile of Bahadur Shah II, was sparked by the rumored use of animal fat in cartridge grease that offended both Hindus and Muslims.

question.leadin: This Indian leader is reputed to have built a terrible prison with the "facade of a spectacular palace."
question.text: Name this son of Bindusara who was famous for his Rock Edicts. This man converted to Buddhism after realizing the atrocities he had committed during his conquest of Kalinga.
question.clue: Some monuments created by this man were inscribed in Brahmi, others were inscribed in Greek.

swap.text: This ruler hid with his son in baskets designated for sweets to escape the clutches of Aurangzeb. More famously, he ripped open the stomach of Afhal Khan after he tried to murder him. This man is known for establishing the Maratha Empire.
swap.clue: A 190-meter statue of this man is under construction 4 kilometers off the coast of a city whose international airport is named for him.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Britain's relations with India, per part.
question.text: John Holwell claimed that 126 Europeans died when placed here after the nawab Siraj-ud-Dawlah forced the surrender of Holwell's garrison.
question.clue: This event's 123 victims primarily died of heat exhaustion in Fort William, where they had been captured by the Nawab of Bengal.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the current India-Pakistan conflict.
swap.text: Discussions have been ongoing between Indian prime minister Atal Behari Vajpayee and this man, the Pakistani president since he overthrew Nawaz Sharif.
swap.clue: This man was the chief architect of the Kargil plan, which was continually rejected by his superiors. After a military coup, he became the tenth president of Pakistan from 2001 to 2008.

question.leadin: One early action by this group was assaulting Patrol Four Four Bravo, kicking off the Black July riots.
question.text: Name this separatist group which sought to create an independent state in Sri Lanka. Pioneers in the use of suicide belts, this group killed Sri Lanka President Premadasa and India Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi in the 1990's.
question.answerHtml: Tamil Tigers [accept LTTE or the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam]
question.clue: This group, based out of Kilinochchi, suffered its final defeat at Mullaitivu.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about amendments to Pakistan's constitution.
swap.text: The first and second amendments to Pakistan's constitution were passed under Zulfikar Ali, a member of this prominent Pakistani political dynasty which runs the Pakistan People's Party.
swap.clue: One member of this family famously stated that his government would "eat grass" if it would help obtain nuclear weapons.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about the Himalayan Kingdoms.
question.text: The Kingdom of Gorkha would be disestablished by Prithvi Narayan Shah in 1768. That ruler would establish this Kingdom in its place, which would last until the 2001 Royal massacre.
question.clue: Chhetris dominated this kingdom's politics, especially after the Kot Massacre reduced its king to a figurehead.

swap.leadin: Kenya's oldest print newspaper was founded by an immigrant from this colony.
swap.text: Give this colony. Immigrants from this colony formed an ambulance corps that helped save lives at the Battle of Spion Kop during the Boer War.
swap.clue: Lord Curzon established this colony's North-West Frontier Province, whose western border was set at the Durand Line to settle the Great Game with Russia.

question.leadin: Name these Muslim polities with historical caste systems.
question.text: The Muslim conquerors who established this sultanate in the 13th century referred to themselves as ashraf, or sons of Muhammad, and eventually split into groups loosely aligned with the local caste system. The last line of rulers of this state came from the Lodi dynasty.
question.clue: This polity's ruling dynasties included the Burji and Khilji, and rulers of this polity including Balban were former slave soldiers known as ghulams.

swap.text: Fellow revolutionary Udham Singh spent 30 years planning to assassinate Michael O'Dwyer for his role in this massacre carried out by British officer Reginald Dyer.
swap.clue: This event led to the "non-cooperation movement" and began as a protest of laws allowing for the denial of jury trials and habeas corpus, the Rowlatt Acts.

question.leadin: This empire's power was broken after its forces, convinced that a British cavalry escort for an ammunition resupply was a flanking maneuver, retreated at the Battle of Ferozeshah (feh-roh-zay-shah).
question.text: Name this major power in the Punjab in the early 19th century, which clashed with forces of the British East India Company in two namesake wars in the 1840s. This highly militaristic empire was founded by Ranjit.
question.clue: Victories at the battles of Attock and Jamrud, among others, brought this empire to its westernmost extent at the expense of the Durrani Empire.

swap.leadin: Antiquarians built Qutb ud-Din Aibak's tomb in this city, where he founded the Delhi Sultanate 20 years after its 1186 siege by Muhammad of Ghor, which ended Ghaznavid rule.
swap.text: Name this city whose tombs of Anarkali and Jahangir were plundered by Ranjit Singh, who made it the Sikh Empire's capital. Mahmud of Ghazni occupied a precursor of this walled city's Mughal fort.
swap.answerHtml: Lahore [or variants of Lahāwar or Rahwar or Lawhūr; accept Lahore Fort; accept Siege of Lahore]
swap.clue: In its earliest years, the Delhi Sultanate was a misnomer, as the Sultanate was actually centered on this city, Pakistan's second largest after Karachi.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a group of people comprised of 36 clans. FTPE.
question.text: Claiming to be descendents of the original Kshatriya, these Hindu peoples held Northern India during the Middle Ages. Their dynasties included the Chauhan and Sisodias, and they were incorporated into the Mughal Empire as part of a marriage-based alliance with Akbar.
question.clue: An entire ruling family of these people called the Guhilas was wiped out in 1303 after the capture of the Chittor Fort.

swap.text: The death of Queen Tripurasundari and the adulthood of a king of this name led to Bhimsen Thapa's fall from power and suicide. A king of this name succeeded his father Raja Raja as second king of the Chola kingdom.
swap.clue: A ruler with this regnal name, his empire's last, died in Pazhayarai in 1279 after submitting to Jatavarman Sundara.
